questions.question_text:
An L-shaped prism has a cross-section made of a bottom rectangle $12$ cm by $2$ cm and an upright column $4$ cm wide reaching a total height of $7$ cm.
The prism is $5$ cm long.
Find its volume.

options.why: Used the full $12\times 7$ rectangle for the cross-section instead of dissecting the L-shape.
Found the cross-sectional area $44$ cm² but forgot to multiply by the $5$ cm length.
Used the full $7$ cm height for the column instead of subtracting the $2$ cm foot, giving column area $4\times 7$.

questions.question_text:
The end of a shed is a pentagon: a $10$ m by $4$ m rectangle with a triangular roof of base $10$ m and height $3$ m on top.
The shed is $6$ m long with this uniform cross-section.
Find its volume.

options.why: Forgot the $\tfrac12$ on the triangle, using $10\times 3$ for the roof instead of $\tfrac{10\times 3}{2}$.
Found the cross-sectional area $55$ m² but did not multiply by the $6$ m length.
Left out the triangular roof entirely and used only the $10\times 4$ rectangle.

questions.question_text:
A T-shaped beam has a cross-section with a top bar $10$ cm wide and $2$ cm thick, and a stem $3$ cm wide and $6$ cm tall below it.
The beam is $8$ cm long.
Find its volume.

options.why: Found the cross-sectional area $38$ cm² but forgot to multiply by the $8$ cm length.
Treated the cross-section as one $10\times 8$ rectangle rather than a T made of a bar and a stem.
Used only the top bar $10\times 2$ and ignored the stem before multiplying by $8$.

questions.question_text:
A concrete edging is a prism whose cross-section is a trapezium with parallel sides $8$ cm and $5$ cm and a perpendicular height of $6$ cm.
The prism is $20$ cm long.
Find its volume.

options.why: Averaged nothing and used $8\times 6$ as the area, treating the trapezium as a rectangle of the longer side.
Forgot the $\div 2$ in the trapezium formula, using $6(8+5)$ for the area.
Found the cross-sectional area $39$ cm² but did not multiply by the $20$ cm length.

questions.question_text:
A prism has a right-angled cross-section like a ramp: it can be split into a $5$ cm by $6$ cm rectangle with a right-angled triangle of base $5$ cm and height $4$ cm on top.
The prism is $9$ cm wide.
Find its volume.

options.why: Forgot the $\tfrac12$ on the triangle, using $5\times 4$ for the triangular part.
Used only the $5\times 6$ rectangle and left out the triangle on top.
Found the cross-sectional area $40$ cm² but did not multiply by the $9$ cm width.

questions.question_text:
A block is a prism formed from a $12$ cm by $8$ cm rectangle with a $5$ cm by $3$ cm rectangular notch cut out of it.
The prism is $4$ cm long.
Find the volume of solid material.

options.why: Used only the full $12\times 8$ rectangle and forgot to subtract the notch.
Added the notch area instead of subtracting it, giving $111\times 4$.
Found the cross-sectional area $81$ cm² but did not multiply by the $4$ cm length.

questions.question_text:
An L-shaped prism has a bottom rectangle $11\text{ cm}$ wide and $3\text{ cm}$ high, with an upright column $2\text{ cm}$ wide reaching a total height of $8\text{ cm}$. The prism is $7\text{ cm}$ long.
Find its volume.

options.why: Used the full column height, giving $(11\times3+2\times8)\times7=343$, and counted the overlap twice.
Treated the cross-section as a full rectangle, giving $11\times8\times7=616$.
Found the cross-sectional area $43\text{ cm}^2$ but did not multiply by the $7\text{ cm}$ length.

questions.solution_text:
Split the cross-section into two rectangles.
$A = (11 \times 3) + (2 \times 5)$
$= 33 + 10$
$= 43\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 43 \times 7$
$= 301\text{ cm}^{3}$

questions.question_text:
A prism has a uniform cross-section made of a rectangle $8\text{ mm}$ wide and $5\text{ mm}$ high on top of a trapezium. The trapezium has parallel sides $8\text{ mm}$ and $14\text{ mm}$ and a perpendicular height of $6\text{ mm}$. The prism is $12\text{ mm}$ long.
Find its volume.

options.why: Forgot to divide the trapezium area by $2$, giving $(40+132)\times12=2064$.
Left out the rectangle and used only the trapezium, giving $66\times12=792$.
Found the cross-sectional area $106\text{ mm}^2$ but did not multiply by the $12\text{ mm}$ length.

questions.solution_text:
Split the cross-section into the rectangle and the trapezium.
$A = (8 \times 5) + \frac{6(8 + 14)}{2}$
$= 40 + 66$
$= 106\text{ mm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 106 \times 12$
$= 1272\text{ mm}^{3}$

questions.question_text:
A pool shell has a level top and is $24\text{ m}$ long and $8\text{ m}$ wide. Its uniform side cross-section has a horizontal floor at a depth of $3\text{ m}$ for the first $6\text{ m}$, then a floor that slopes upwards to a depth of $1\text{ m}$ at the other end.
Find the volume of earth that must be excavated for the shell to fit exactly.

options.why: Used the full $3\text{ m}$ depth throughout, giving $24\times3\times8=576$.
Used all $24\text{ m}$ for the sloping section as well as the $6\text{ m}$ flat section, giving $(6\times3+24(3+1)/2)\times8=528$.
Left out the flat deep section and used only the sloping section, giving $18(3+1)/2\times8=288$.

questions.solution_text:
Split the side cross-section into a rectangle and a trapezium.
The sloping section is $24 - 6 = 18\text{ m}$ long.
$A = (6 \times 3) + \frac{18(3 + 1)}{2}$
$= 18 + 36$
$= 54\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 54 \times 8$
$= 432\text{ m}^{3}$
